dimensions.assessment: Affects foreign persons or entities determined to have diverted or destroyed U.S. humanitarian assistance.
dimensions.evidence: any foreign person or entity the Secretary of State determines is responsible for the unauthorized diversion or destruction of United States humanitarian assistance... is liable

dimensions.assessment: Makes responsible parties financially liable to the United States for the full value of the diverted or destroyed assistance.
dimensions.evidence: is liable to the United States for the value of the assistance the Secretary determines was so diverted or destroyed.

dimensions.assessment: Permits the recovery and crediting of funds back to Department of State or federal agency accounts, though amounts depend on future recoveries.
dimensions.evidence: any funds received by the Secretary of State pursuant to a determination under this section may be credited to an appropriate account

dimensions.assessment: Creates a new statutory liability and recovery mechanism for diverted or destroyed humanitarian assistance without amending a specific prior act's text.
dimensions.evidence: To ensure that persons found responsible for the unauthorized diversion or destruction of United States humanitarian assistance are liable to the United States

dimensions.assessment: Permanent establishment of liability and fund recovery rules.
dimensions.evidence: Notwithstanding any other provision of law or regulation, any foreign person or entity... is liable

missing_information: The total monetary value of humanitarian assistance currently subject to unauthorized diversion or destruction.
The likelihood or amount of funds successfully recovered.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes legal liability for foreign persons or entities responsible for the unauthorized diversion or destruction of U.S. humanitarian assistance, allowing the State Department to recover funds.
